q: Ludhiana's knitwear MSMEs: what do their boilers burn, and what will export buyers ask for?
title: Ludhiana knitwear boilers and buyer data
short: Wood, rice husk, pet coke and diesel, raising steam for dyeing yarn and fabric, across a cluster of about 14,000 MSMEs, 70% of them micro. Export buyers ask for fuel and power use by month, Scope 1 and 2 totals, and output, so pet coke against husk is the choice that moves your number most.
audience: Knitwear makers, dyers and processors in Ludhiana selling to export brands or exporters

ul: About 14,000 MSME units: 9,800 micro, 2,800 small and 1,400 medium.
Knitwear makers and exporters at the core, backed by spinners, dyers and job knitters.
Dyeing, processing and spinning units use the most energy; printing uses less.
Electricity runs compressors, motors and lighting. Steam for dyeing comes from boilers burning wood, rice husk, pet coke or HSD.

sections.h: What a buyer's supplier form usually asks
ul: Fuel burnt each month by type, in tonnes or litres, and electricity in kWh, for the last full year.
Scope 1 and Scope 2 totals in tonnes CO2e, and the factors used.
Output in kg or pieces, so they can work out a figure per unit.
Any solar or renewable power, with bills or certificates.
For biomass: where it comes from and whether it is a residue, such as husk, or wood.

sections.h: How each boiler fuel is counted
ul: Pet coke and HSD: fossil CO2 in Scope 1. Pet coke is about 3.17 t CO2 per tonne on IPCC defaults.
Rice husk and wood: the CO2 is biogenic and reported separately, outside the scopes. Methane and nitrous oxide from burning stay in Scope 1, a few tonnes CO2e per 100 t.
Buying steam from a neighbour: Scope 2, using the supplier's fuel data.

ol: Collect 12 months of fuel bills and weighbridge slips for husk, wood and coke, and every power bill.
Note boiler-house stock at each month end, so you count fuel burnt, not fuel bought.
Record kg of fabric dyed or pieces made each month.
Keep a supplier note for husk or wood showing its source.
Fix boiler losses first: SIDBI-supported energy audits in the cluster found boilers the biggest saving: an estimated Rs 26.6 lakh a year at one unit for a Rs 4.5 lakh investment.

example.title: Worked example: 100 t of pet coke against 100 t of rice husk
lines: Pet coke: 100 t x 32.5 GJ per t = 3.25 TJ x 97.5 t CO2 per TJ = 317 t CO2 in Scope 1
Rice husk: 100 t x 11.6 GJ per t = 1.16 TJ
Husk methane: 1.16 x 30 kg = 34.8 kg x 27 = 0.94 t CO2e; nitrous oxide: 1.16 x 4 kg = 4.6 kg x 273 = 1.27 t CO2e
Husk Scope 1: about 2.2 t CO2e; biogenic CO2 reported separately: 1.16 x 100 = 116 t
Husk gives less heat per tonne, so you need about 2.8 t of husk for the heat of 1 t of pet coke; even then Scope 1 stays near 6 t against 317
example.note: IPCC 2006 default net calorific values and factors for manufacturing, with AR6 warming potentials (27 for non-fossil methane, 273 for nitrous oxide). Use your fuel's own lab values if you have them.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and power bills into a monthly record traced to each document, so the fuel, power and Scope 1 and 2 figures a buyer's form asks for come from your own papers.
